name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba

background.fact: Born February 14, 2002 in Nacogdoches, Texas, and raised in Rockwall, Texas, where he attended Rockwall High School.

In his junior year at Rockwall he had 97 catches for 1,828 yards and 20 touchdowns; as a senior 104 catches for 2,094 yards and 35 touchdowns. He was Texas Gatorade Football Player of the Year and a five-star recruit who chose Ohio State.
At Ohio State he set a school record with 1,606 receiving yards in 2021, including 347 yards in the 2022 Rose Bowl (an FBS bowl record).
Seattle drafted him 20th overall in the first round of the 2023 NFL draft. He became a starter in his second season (1,130 yards, first Pro Bowl).
In 2025 he led the NFL with 1,793 receiving yards on 119 catches, a Seahawks franchise record, won Offensive Player of the Year, and helped Seattle win Super Bowl LX.
Listed at 6 ft 0 in, 197 lb, age 24, jersey 11, in his fourth NFL season.

background.fact: Career regular season through Week 9 of 2026: 60 games, 353 catches, 4,587 yards and 29 touchdowns.

family.fact: Parents are firefighter Maada and high school teacher Jami Smith, who later divorced; his father put him and older brother Canaan through daily sports workouts. Canaan is a former professional baseball player.

He added "Njigba" to his surname in high school to honor his grandfather John, who died in 2014. His paternal grandparents are from Sierra Leone and he wears that country's flag on the back of his helmet.

scouts_read: Smith-Njigba looks healthy and set to play, so the question is quarterback and script, not availability. Darnold is reported out, and the one game he had with Lock in Week 9 was his worst of the year at 51 yards. Even so, Lock-throwing games produced both his best and worst weeks, and his 99 targets show he is the first read. Las Vegas is reported to be soft against the run, which could let Seattle lean on Wilson and trim his volume. I would project a decent game near 16 to 18 points with a real chance of a big day if Lock throws often.
